sections.h2: Painting a business without closing it
body: A shop or restaurant in Historic Downtown depends on foot traffic, and a week of closed doors hurts. Our commercial painting in Dunnellon, FL works around your open sign, which can mean evenings, overnight shifts, or a weekend push. Dining rooms can be painted after close and ready for the next service. Exteriors are done in sections so the entry and signage stay visible, usually after a storefront soft wash clears the grime.

bullets: Multi-family rentals, HOA common areas, and managed properties
body: For restaurant-specific concerns like grease, odors, and turnaround, see our retail and restaurant painting page.

Some of Dunnellon's commercial buildings share the age and materials of the historic homes around them. Old wood trim, multiple paint layers, and weathered masonry need the same patient prep: scraping to a sound edge, priming bare surfaces, and choosing breathable coatings. On masonry, a limewash or a high-build coating can freshen a facade while respecting its character. Signs of water getting behind the surface are covered in our article on hidden siding moisture damage.

sections.h2: Interior finishes that hold up to the public
body: Commercial interiors take far more contact than homes. Corridors, restrooms, and dining rooms need scrub-resistant finishes that can be cleaned daily without burnishing. Door frames and handrails get a urethane enamel that resists chipping. Where a business wants a calm, consistent look across several rooms, we standardize colors and sheens and record them so future touch-ups match. Low-VOC products are available for spaces that have to reopen quickly.

Licensed, bonded, and fully insured in Florida, we carry workers' comp on every crew member and can issue a certificate of insurance naming your company, HOA, or management firm before we mobilize. Our own crews do the work, with one crew lead as your point of contact from walkthrough to final punch list.
Bids are itemized by area and surface, with products named and a schedule attached, which makes it easy to phase work by budget or tenant turnover. Nothing is added later without written approval.

Storefront exteriors follow the same weather calendar as homes, with October through May the easiest window. Summer work starts at first light and wraps before the afternoon storms. Sidewalks are coned off in sections, and we coordinate with you on deliveries and parking.

Commercial jobs often include concrete and masonry painting, epoxy or polyaspartic floor coatings, waterproofing, and anti-graffiti coatings on exposed walls. These can be added to the same scope. See our full commercial painting service, or go back to the Dunnellon contractor page.

faqs.q: Can you paint my restaurant overnight?
faqs.a: Yes. Commercial work can be scheduled at night or on weekends so you can open on time.

faqs.q: Can you provide a certificate of insurance before starting?
faqs.a: Yes. Tell us the exact entity name at the walkthrough, and the certificate will be in your hands before the first crew arrives.

faqs.q: Do you paint rental units between tenants?
faqs.a: Yes. Multi-family and rental turnovers are part of our commercial work, and the scope can be standardized across units.
